title: Crypto’s bear market, tech’s correction: what our experts see
summary: Bitcoin hit a four-month low near USD 62k and tech stocks are sliding. Bear market or correction? Read what our CoinShares experts see in our latest market analysis.
body_markdown:
November has been rough for digital assets and technology stocks. Bitcoin fell to a four-month low near USD 62k on 14 Nov 2026, and equities have sold off since Jensen Huang’s resignation as Nvidia’s chief executive. Is this a bear market, or a correction? We asked our Head of Research, James Butterfill, and our Index Fund Manager, Alexandre Schmidt, for their readings. Both views and mentioned data date from 18 Nov 2026.


## Crypto: a continuation, not a new start


Is this volatility an opportunity or the sign of a bear market? We asked our Head of Research James Butterfill and our Index Equity Analyst Alexandre Schmidt their takes on the current situation. A note provided on Wednesday 18 November 2026.


For James Butterfill, the view is clear: Bitcoin was already in a bear market. “I see this as a continuation of the existing bear market rather than the start of another,” he says. “Bitcoin is still working through the whale selling that weighed on prices from late 2025, while expectations of higher interest rates and weakness in technology stocks have kept buyers cautious. Our base case remains range trading around USD 60k to 90k through much of 2027, until falling inflation gives monetary policy room to ease. Geopolitics will have a considerable say in that. A sustained breakout would likely require a change in the policy outlook, renewed whale participation or both.”


As he wrote in our latest 13F report, which compiles the quarterly holdings disclosures of US institutional investors, “Institutional adoption continues”, yet “it cannot cancel out restrictive liquidity.”


## Equities: a correction, with crypto-linked shares as the exception


In equities the picture is more nuanced, because valuations remain high. “Sentiment in equity markets has turned negative in recent weeks following concerns about the financing capabilities of major players in the AI trade, currently one of the main sources of US growth. While Jensen Huang’s departure from Nvidia has thrown further uncertainty into the mix, the sell-off has so far been deemed a correction, with lofty valuations prevailing throughout,” Alexandre Schmidt says. “Broader equities remain in positive territory, with the S&P 500 up 7% YTD, but blockchain-related names are feeling the pressure, with bellwether names such as Coinbase and Strategy down 49% and 36% YTD respectively (as of 18 November 2026).”


That gap is the point: blockchain-related shares are trading with crypto, not with the wider market. “Given that blockchain equity fundamentals are closely related to that of cryptocurrency markets, a breakout is likely to be triggered by an appreciation in Bitcoin and other digital assets or broader adoption of blockchain technology in other applications, especially asset tokenisation,” Schmidt adds. “Put simply, blockchain equities’ bear market is a mirror of crypto’s, and it is likely to end only when crypto sees a path to a sustained recovery.”


Both researchers point to the same hinge: a change in the outlook for crypto itself, whether from policy, from large holders returning, or from wider use of blockchain technology.
